cards.front: day
cards.back: The time when it is light because our part of the Earth faces the Sun.
cards.say: day. The time when it is light because our part of the Earth faces the Sun.

cards.front: night
cards.back: The time when it is dark because our part of the Earth faces away from the Sun.
cards.say: night. The time when it is dark because our part of the Earth faces away from the Sun.

cards.front: spin
cards.back: To turn round and round. The Earth spins.
cards.say: spin. To turn round and round. The Earth spins.

cards.front: axis
cards.back: An imaginary line through the Earth. The Earth spins round it.
cards.say: axis. An imaginary line through the Earth. The Earth spins round it.

cards.front: sunrise
cards.back: When the Sun first comes up in the morning.
cards.say: sunrise. When the Sun first comes up in the morning.

cards.front: sunset
cards.back: When the Sun goes down in the evening.
cards.say: sunset. When the Sun goes down in the evening.

cards.front: What causes day and night?
cards.back: The Earth spins, so our part faces the Sun, then away from it.
cards.say: What causes day and night? The Earth spins, so our part faces the Sun, then away from it.

cards.front: How long does it take the Earth to spin once?
cards.back: About 24 hours, which is one day and one night.
cards.say: How long does it take the Earth to spin once? About 24 hours, which is one day and one night.

cards.front: Does the Sun move round the Earth?
cards.back: No. It only looks that way because the Earth spins.
cards.say: Does the Sun move round the Earth? No. It only looks that way because the Earth spins.

cards.front: Which way does the Sun seem to rise from?
cards.back: The east.
cards.say: Which way does the Sun seem to rise from? The east.

cards.front: Which way does the Sun seem to set?
cards.back: The west.
cards.say: Which way does the Sun seem to set? The west.

cards.front: When is it day on one side of the Earth?
cards.back: When that side faces the Sun.
cards.say: When is it day on one side of the Earth? When that side faces the Sun.

cards.front: Is the Sun a star?
cards.back: Yes. It is the star closest to the Earth.
cards.say: Is the Sun a star? Yes. It is the star closest to the Earth.

cards.front: What shines at night?
cards.back: The stars and the Moon.
cards.say: What shines at night? The stars and the Moon.

cards.front: Does the Moon make its own light?
cards.back: No. It reflects light from the Sun.
cards.say: Does the Moon make its own light? No. It reflects light from the Sun.

cards.front: Why is it dark at night?
cards.back: Our part of the Earth faces away from the Sun.
cards.say: Why is it dark at night? Our part of the Earth faces away from the Sun.

cards.front: What does the Earth do in one day?
cards.back: It spins round once.
cards.say: What does the Earth do in one day? It spins round once.

cards.front: How long is a day and a night together?
cards.back: 24 hours.
cards.say: How long is a day and a night together? 24 hours.

cards.front: What do we call the time when the Sun comes up?
cards.back: Sunrise.
cards.say: What do we call the time when the Sun comes up? Sunrise.

cards.front: What do we call the time when the Sun goes down?
cards.back: Sunset.
cards.say: What do we call the time when the Sun goes down? Sunset.

cards.front: Is the Earth still or spinning?
cards.back: Spinning. We cannot feel it.
cards.say: Is the Earth still or spinning? Spinning. We cannot feel it.
